key_insight: AIPatient Arena evaluates medical LLMs in realistic, multi-turn EHR-grounded consultations and shows that strong chat performance does not guarantee strong clinical reasoning.
clinical_relevance: This framework can help healthcare teams and developers assess whether a model can safely gather, interpret, and explain patient information before deployment.
method: Built patient-specific knowledge graphs from EHR data to drive multi-turn physician-patient interactions.
Scored LLMs across eight clinical competence dimensions, including questioning, ethics, explanation, integration, medication safety, ambiguity handling, coverage, and diagnosis.
Tested on one primary cohort and two out-of-distribution validation cohorts to probe robustness.
evidence_signal: The study evaluated 437 primary patients plus 119 and 67 out-of-distribution patients, finding high scores for questioning and ethics but weaker performance in ambiguity handling, information coverage, and diagnostic reasoning.
watch_item: Final-answer accuracy alone may overestimate readiness; recurrent failures like repetitive questioning and missed past history suggest workflow-level testing is still necessary.
paper_title: AIPatient Arena: EHR-grounded evaluation of large language models in end-to-end clinical consultation workflows
